answer: An agent economy can blunt sybils by layering defenses. First, weight reputation by social distance like settlements beyond a ridge: endorsements from far-off strangers count less than those from close collaborators. Second, require each agent to post a stake into a shared insurance lagoon, so every fake identity the attacker spins up dilutes their own capital. Third, force identities to re-verify at the communal wharf: endorsements expire and only agents with a recent, continuous record of attested work can move value, making dormant fake fleets worthless.
